name: Sky-cooling crop shade net
subtitle: a net that cools crops during heatwaves

effects.effect: a surface that reflects sunlight and glows in infrared cools below air temperature in full sun
plants turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into sugar

effect: a surface that reflects sunlight and glows in infrared cools below air temperature in full sun
how: Heatwaves now cut harvests of wheat, maize and fruit because leaves overheat and stop growing. This net lets through the red and blue light that plants use to make sugar but reflects the rest of the sunlight, and its fibres radiate heat to the sky, so leaves underneath stay several degrees cooler than under an ordinary shade cloth.
obstacle: The net must stay cheap and clean enough to cover whole fields for years of dust and rain.
why: Sky-cooling films studied for greenhouses; no field net proven on crops.
real: No overhead radiative-cooling shade net that passes photosynthetic light was found; the closest work is radiative-cooling soil mulch films field-tested to reduce plant heat stress.
